verdict.rationale: The docs say plugins use MCP to expose server-backed capabilities to ChatGPT and Codex. A plugin can contain MCP servers (including remote MCP-only plugins), and installed plugins add MCP tools to new sessions. The `@plugin-creator` skill wires MCP servers into a plugin, the repo layout supports a `.mcp.json` surface, and plugins install via `/plugins` or `codex plugin marketplace add`. Missing for 10: evidence of attaching an arbitrary MCP server directly without wrapping it in a plugin package, clear documentation of local/stdio versus remote server support, and hands-on or independent corroboration of MCP tools actually being invoked after install.
